programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Beach shoes have gone missing and red hair is found at the scene - Grumblestunk is blaming Stan! Who really did it? Stan and Gran spy a mystery! Tha brògan traghad air a dhol a dhìth; tha falt ruadh ga lorg aig an làraich 's tha Greannarlobht a' coireachadh Dan! Ach cò tha cionntach? Tha rùn-dìomhair ro Dan is Gran!

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri coineanach agus tìgear! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like a rabbit and a tiger!

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Air latha fliuch, tha plòigh aig na Losgannan a’ dèanamh dealbh-chluich faileasan. On a rainy day, the Froglets have fun making a shadow show for Bertie and puppet friends.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Nuair tha Bèibidh Dràgon Brot’ a’ cluich geama le Beag is Meanbh, tha e 'g ionnsachadh gu bheil co-roinneadh spòrsail. When Baby Soup Dragan is playing with Small and Tiny, he learns that sharing is a lot of fun.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Beag Clangair 'g ionnsachadh an-diugh gu bheil barrachd a thaobh Granaidh na shaoileadh tu! Small Clanger learns that there is more to Granny than you’d think!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Abigail NicÌomhair a’ leughadh Balach anns na Sgòthan. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh is a dhealbhachadh le Greg Stobbs agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. Abigail Maciver reads Balach anns na Sgòthan, written and illustrated by Greg Stobbs and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Tha tòrr aig Zala ri ionnsachadh mu thrufailean. Le taic bho a nàbaidh, Sara, agus Pùpa, an cuilean, tha i airson trufailean a lorg gus am faigh i air pasta traidiseanta le trufail ullachadh airson na caraidean aice. Zala has much to learn about truffles. With assistance from her neighbour, Sara, and Pùpa the puppy, she goes in search of truffles so that she can prepare a traditional pasta dish with truffles for her friends.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Sebastian a' dol air ais air a ghealladh, taic a thoirt dha Adele leis a' phròiseact aice, chan eil i air a dòigh leis idir, idir. Tha gnothaichean rudeigin fionnar an dèidh sin! When Sebastian goes back on his promise to support Adele with her project, she is not happy with him at all. Things are a bit chilly from then onwards.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: 'S e cò-là breith Timmy a th' ann agus tha an Treud a' cur pàrtaidh air dòigh dha. An toiseach, tha an gnothaich a' còrdadh ris ach nuair a tha e air fhàgail leis fhèin, cò aig tha fios dè thachras...... It's Timmy's birthday, and the flock have thrown a party for him. At first he's delighted by all the attention, but when the flock become distracted and he's left with no-one to play with, he decides to entertain himself.

programme.title: Uaine
programme.desc: Aon rud nach eil gann an Alba, ‘s e sin gaoth agus tha Calum air iomall baile Ghlaschu aig Tuathanas Gaoithe Whitelee gus barrachd fhaighinn a-mach mu chumhachd na gaoithe. Ach tha ceist chudromach aige dhuinn: am b’ urrainn do bhraidhm muileann-gaoithe a thionndadh? One thing we’re not short of in Scotland is wind and Calum is on the outskirts of Glasgow to find out more about wind power.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Teirm ùr aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche agus tha Mgr Mackle, Ceannard na Sgoile, a’ cur fàilte air na sgoilearan agus na tidsearan. Chì sinn dè mar a thèid dhaibh le na camarathan a’ leantainn na rudan craicte a bhios a’ tachairt san sgoil. It’s the start of a new term at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche and headmaster Mr Mackle welcomes teachers and pupils back to the school. We see how they get on as our cameras observe the crazy goings-on.

programme.title: Co-Sheirm
programme.desc: Sreath bhon tasglann a' taisbeanadh còisirean is guthan sònraichte. Anns a' phrògram seo, Còisir Ghàidhlig Ìleach Ghlaschu. Archive series spotlighting choirs and outstanding soloists - this episode features The Glasgow Islay Gaelic Choir.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Fine Mayer, who grew up in Germany, chats to Joy in the studio, and a hungry Calum Maclean is on a quest for a famous mouth-watering soup in Morayshire.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Port Steòrnabhaigh
programme.desc: Based in the main port in the Hebrides, we follow the beating hearts of Stornoway Harbour. In her shelter, there is a bustling community to be found. In this episode, there is a health problem on board a boat that has come alongside, and we get a look at the progress of the new Deep Water Terminal. Stèidhte ann am prìomh port nan Eilean Siar, the sinne a’ leantainn cridhe Port Steòrnabhaigh. Na fasgadh, tha coimhearsnachd trang ri lorg. Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha suidheachadh slàinte air bòrd bàta a tha a’ tighinn gu cala, agus gheibh sinn sealladh air adhartas a’ Chalaidh Dhomhain ùr. Thig còmhla rinn ‘s sinn a’ leanntainn beatha ann am Port Steòrnabhaigh.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: From the shores of the Hebrides to the bright lights of Washington DC, this documentary reveals the footballing journey of Lewis man Ally ‘Bubble’ Mackay.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Tha dùbhlain ris nach robh dùil aig Coinneach MacFhraing agus Somhairle Mac Iain ri làimhseachadh agus iad a’ sireadh cuairt-dànachd air Costa Blanca na Spàinn. Coinneach Rankin and Somhairle Johnston face unexpected challenges in their search for adventure on Spain’s Costa Blanca. A’ dèiligeadh ri dùbhlain ris nach robh dùil air oirthir na Meadhan-thìreach, tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ tighinn tarsaing air suidheachaidhean doirbh agus e a’ dèiligeadh ri ballachan creige àrda Costa Blanca na Spàinn. Tha Somhairle Mac Iain a’ faighinn a-mach carson a tha na beanntan os cionn Baile Benidorm a’ tàladh rothaichean bho air feadh na Roinn Eòrpa, agus ag ionnsachadh mar a làimhsicheas e eagal ann an suidheachaidhean duilich. Facing unpredictable challenges on the Mediterranean coast, Coinneach Rankin encounters difficult circumstances as he tackles the towering rock walls of Spain’s Costa Blanca. Somhairle Johnston discovers why the mountains inland of Benidorm have long attracted cyclists from all over Europe and learns how to manage fear in tough situations.

programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: Leis gu bheil e a-nis slàn, fallain às dèidh ionnsachadh bho chionn còrr is bliadhna gu bheil a chridhe a’ fàiligeadh, tha Ruairidh, cuide ri Ùisdean, ag ullachadh measgachadh de shoithichean mar dhòigh taing a thoirt do dhithis dhen na nursaichean a bh’ aige. Tha Ruairidh a’ dèanamh Bonnaich Crùbaig Baltimore, Pàidh Ùbhlan gun Siùcar no Bathar-bainne, airson a ghabhail le Reòiteag gun Bhathar-bainne. Tha Ùisdean, a tha cinnteach gu bheil feum aig Ruairidh air pàirtean a bharrachd, a’ dèanamh Cridhe Daimh air a lìonadh le Càl-bloinigein agus Duxelles Balgain-buachrach. Tha e cuideachd a’ dèanamh soitheach blasta le Breac-garbh agus Beurre Blanc. Having thankfully been given a clean bill of health after Roddy's heart failure diagnosis over a year ago, he and Uisdean prepare a selection of dishes as a small thank you to two of his nurses. Roddy prepares Baltimore crab cakes, a dairy and sugar-free apple pie to be accompanied with dairy-free ice cream! Uisdean, convinced that Roddy might need a spare part, prepares ox heart stuffed with spinach and mushroom duxelles. For a tasty fish dish, he cooks up halibut with Bleurre blanc. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Prògram aithriseach ciùil le Julie Fowlis is Muireann NicAmhlaoibh 's iad air slighe rannsachadh mu na freumhan aca fhèin. Nì iadsan siubhal thar chrìochan 's thar chleachdaidhean eadar taobh siar na h-Èirinn agus Eileanan Siar na h-Alba, a' coinneachadh, a'conaltradh 's a cluich ceòl air an t-slighe. An t-seachdain-sa chì sinn Julie agus Muireann ann an caochladh àiteachan a tha ainmeil airson òrain, ceòl agus beul-aithris agus a'feitheamh airson fàilte chridheil a chur orra, tha eòlaichean ciùil, pìobairean agus seinneadairean, nam measg Gillebrìde Mac Ille Mhaoil ann an Uibhist agus Daoirí Farrell ann a Baile-Atha-Cliath. Musical documentary, presented by Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh in which they explore their shared musical heritage. Julie and Muireann cross borders and traditions from the Western Isles to the west coast of Ireland, meeting and making music en route. In this episode, Julie and Muireann visit several locations synonymous with folk song, music and folklore. Welcoming them to each destination are musicians, pipers and singers, including Gillebrìde MacMillan in Uist and Daoirí Farrell in Dublin.

Three avid chess players take on a trio unified by their love of mathematics as they compete for the glory of third place in the series, trying to draw together the connections between elements which, at first glance, seem utterly random.

programme.title: Art on the BBC
programme.desc: Often dismissed as a chocolate box painter in his day, Constable is now acknowledged to have been a revolutionary. Art historian Rose Balston explores six decades of BBC archive to discover how TV has influenced our understanding of him. Constable pushed the boundaries of landscape painting to such an extent that he was rejected by the establishment. Perhaps just as surprisingly, he poured his love for one woman onto the canvas as no painter of landscapes had done before. This programme goes beyond cliché to discover what the BBC archive has to say about a much misunderstood English master.

programme.title: Universe
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox begins his epic exploration of the cosmos with a hymn to the great luminous bodies that bring light and warmth to the universe: the stars. It is estimated that there are two hundred trillion stars in the universe, each playing their part in an epic story of creation - a great saga that stretches from the dawn of time, with the arrival of the first star, through diverse generations until the arrival of our own star, the sun, and a civilisation that has grown up in its light.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Laurence Rees's landmark 1997 series explored the reasons why Germany fell in thrall to the Nazis. Combining astonishing archive, storytelling and interviews with figures at the heart of Hitler’s rise to power, it tells us of the Nazi mentality and the reasons behind their beliefs. Chillingly, it looks at those who still think the Nazis were right. Rees is an author and broadcaster, perfectly placed to look back at the series he wrote and produced. He tells us of the origins of the series - how the fall of the Berlin Wall opened possibilities for interviews with people who previously had been unreachable. He recalls the powerful moments when some of those closely associated with the horrors were challenged. And he explains how the regime rose out of chaos, both in Germany and within the Nazis themselves. Join Laurence as he takes us behind the scenes of this award-winning series that has resonance to this day.

programme.title: The Nazis: A Warning from History
programme.desc: How was it possible that the cultured nation at the heart of Europe ever allowed Hitler to come to power? With the help of film archive discoveries from Russia and interviews with eyewitnesses, many of whom are former members of the Nazi party and have never appeared on television before, this film reveals how the Nazi party was born and grew in support in the late 1920s, and shows just why in January 1933 Germany's President Hindenburg appointed a new popular chancellor who was openly committed to overthrowing German democracy - Adolf Hitler. Hitler's personality was to dominate the Nazi party. But eyewitnesses have very different recollections of his effect upon them. To Nazi supporter Fridolin von Spaun 'the long gaze which he gave me convinced me completely that he was a man with honourable intentions.' But to German diplomat Herbert Richter, who saw Hitler in the 1920s, 'he wasn't quite normal. He was spooky.' The Nazis wanted the world to believe that Hitler's rise to power was inevitable - this programme shatters that myth.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Ken Loach reflects on The Old Oak, his deeply moving portrait of solidarity, displacement and community in a former mining village in County Durham. Set against the arrival of Syrian refugees in a town scarred by austerity and deindustrialisation, the film explores whether compassion and collective action can survive in fractured times.

programme.title: The Old Oak
programme.desc: A pub landlord in a previously thriving mining community in County Durham struggles to hold on to his pub and keep it as the one remaining public space people can meet in the town. Meanwhile, tensions rise in the town when Syrian refugees are placed there.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Ken Loach discusses Up the Junction, his landmark 1965 contribution to the BBC’s The Wednesday Play strand, adapted from Nell Dunn’s celebrated stories of working-class life in Battersea. Blending drama with documentary realism, the production shocked audiences with its frank depiction of sex, illegal abortion and everyday poverty, attracting record complaints while redefining television drama in Britain.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s buyer fell in love with the Lake District as a child and feels that now the time is right to finally make her dream move there. Sonali Shah is on hand with a selection of gorgeous cottages in some of the region’s most sought-after villages, including a one-of-a-kind mystery house.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor form a plan that might finally bring their hunt for Jamie to an end, but they can’t do it alone. Pip is forced to swallow her pride and ask Cara for help. The gang split up and launch a daring breaking-and-entering mission. Pip is left exposed and isolated as she faces the person behind Jamie’s disappearance. A complicated truth emerges, and once again, Pip must accept that the line between good and evil is murky. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. Her closest friends try to provide support, but Pip needs time. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Grab a cuppa and join Danny Sebastian as he brews up a special show all about tea and the history of tea drinking. Time to get the kettle on!

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor form a plan that might finally bring their hunt for Jamie to an end, but they can’t do it alone. Pip is forced to swallow her pride and ask Cara for help. The gang split up and launch a daring breaking-and-entering mission. Pip is left exposed and isolated as she faces the person behind Jamie’s disappearance. A complicated truth emerges, and once again, Pip must accept that the line between good and evil is murky. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. Her closest friends try to provide support, but Pip needs time. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

The gang split up and launch a daring breaking-and-entering mission. Pip is left exposed and isolated as she faces the person behind Jamie’s disappearance. A complicated truth emerges, and once again, Pip must accept that the line between good and evil is murky. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. Her closest friends try to provide support, but Pip needs time. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Grab a cuppa and join Danny Sebastian as he brews up a special show all about tea and the history of tea drinking. In Eastbourne, Danny is serenaded by organist Chris Mannion as they reminisce about tea dances, while in Hastings, Danny is given a tea-tastic masterclass by etiquette expert Rebecca Gildea. On his journey along the south coast of England, Danny stirs up memories of bygone buys on Bargain Hunt, from caddy spoons to biscuit tins, and at the end of the show, he counts down the most profitable tea-related antiques and collectibles. Time to get the kettle on!

programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc: A haul of suspected cannabis plants is found at a residential home, stolen bike parts are discovered in a derelict hotel, and dogs sniff out drugs at the airport.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson takes fellow actor Jo Joyner horse riding near the small town of Wooler as he introduces her to his beloved Northumberland. The Cheviots provide a stunning backdrop at the riding centre at Kimmerton - where Jo gets back in the saddle for the first time in years. With her love of riding renewed, Robson takes Jo to Heatherslaw Mill for an outdoor cookery lesson to make soda bread.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s buyer fell in love with the Lake District as a child and feels that now the time is right to finally make her dream move there. Sonali Shah is on hand with a selection of gorgeous cottages in some of the region’s most sought-after villages, including a one-of-a-kind mystery house.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s buyer fell in love with the Lake District as a child and feels that now the time is right to finally make her dream move there. Sonali Shah is on hand with a selection of gorgeous cottages in some of the region’s most sought-after villages, including a one-of-a-kind mystery house.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

Sonali Shah is on hand with a selection of gorgeous cottages in some of the region’s most sought-after villages, including a one-of-a-kind mystery house.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor form a plan that might finally bring their hunt for Jamie to an end, but they can’t do it alone. Pip is forced to swallow her pride and ask Cara for help. The gang split up and launch a daring breaking-and-entering mission. Pip is left exposed and isolated as she faces the person behind Jamie’s disappearance. A complicated truth emerges, and once again, Pip must accept that the line between good and evil is murky. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. Her closest friends try to provide support, but Pip needs time. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor form a plan that might finally bring their hunt for Jamie to an end, but they can’t do it alone. Pip is forced to swallow her pride and ask Cara for help. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. Her closest friends try to provide support, but Pip needs time. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor form a plan that might finally bring their hunt for Jamie to an end, but they can’t do it alone. Pip is forced to swallow her pride and ask Cara for help. The gang split up and launch a daring breaking-and-entering mission. Pip is left exposed and isolated as she faces the person behind Jamie’s disappearance. A complicated truth emerges, and once again, Pip must accept that the line between good and evil is murky. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Grab a cuppa and join Danny Sebastian as he brews up a special show all about tea and the history of tea drinking. In Eastbourne, Danny is serenaded by organist Chris Mannion as they reminisce about tea dances, while in Hastings, Danny is given a tea-tastic masterclass by etiquette expert Rebecca Gildea. On his journey along the south coast of England, Danny stirs up memories of bygone buys on Bargain Hunt, from caddy spoons to biscuit tins, and at the end of the show, he counts down the most profitable tea-related antiques and collectibles. Time to get the kettle on!

programme.title: Policing Paradise

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson takes fellow actor Jo Joyner horse riding near the small town of Wooler as he introduces her to his beloved Northumberland. The Cheviots provide a stunning backdrop at the riding centre at Kimmerton - where Jo gets back in the saddle for the first time in years. With her love of riding renewed, Robson takes Jo to Heatherslaw Mill for an outdoor cookery lesson to make soda bread.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Today’s buyer fell in love with the Lake District as a child and feels that now the time is right to finally make her dream move there. Sonali Shah is on hand with a selection of gorgeous cottages in some of the region’s most sought-after villages, including a one-of-a-kind mystery house.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor return to the abandoned manor at night hoping for answers, but nothing they uncover makes sense. The arrival of two mysterious figures leads to a dangerous chase. Despite it resulting in a promising discovery, tension mounts between the gang. At court, the deliberation is brief, and the verdict comes sooner than anyone expects. Back at school, the pressure finally boils over. Pip loses control, earning herself a suspension. Pip’s parents and Ravi are unable to comfort her. Connor delivers news that brings the search for Jamie to an abrupt and indefinite halt. Spiralling and inconsolable, Pip takes advice from an unlikely person and is inspired to act. Later, Pip meets Ravi, and they are finally able to have an honest conversation. When a new lead emerges, the group regain momentum with renewed determination, and a crucial clue cracks the case wide open.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip, Ravi and Connor form a plan that might finally bring their hunt for Jamie to an end, but they can’t do it alone. Pip is forced to swallow her pride and ask Cara for help. The gang split up and launch a daring breaking-and-entering mission. Pip is left exposed and isolated as she faces the person behind Jamie’s disappearance. A complicated truth emerges, and once again, Pip must accept that the line between good and evil is murky. A deadly encounter unfolds that will change Pip’s life forever and cause shock waves throughout Little Kilton. In the aftermath, Pip struggles to make peace with the fallout of yet another case. Her closest friends try to provide support, but Pip needs time. With unfinished business still lingering around Max Hastings, Pip knows that she won’t be able to rest until she finds a way to bring him down.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo Headlam and Joe Swift are in Wilmslow to help Vin and Reena transform their chaotic patch of grass, gravel and concrete into a zen and grow-your-own garden for family healing. With a pile of old bricks where a shed once stood and a path that leads nowhere, the couple have struggled to create the sanctuary they long for. They dream of a peaceful space with a cosy pergola and decking for family time, a fire pit for evenings together and a vegetable bed to grow organic produce to support Vin’s health. A tree to honour their ancestors and a family swing for their daughter Pruthvi will add meaning and magic, while a small play area ensures fun for all. Both Vin and Reena share a deep love of nature and spirituality. With Vin living with Crohn’s disease, healthy eating and time outdoors are vital to family life. Can the team deliver the calm, nourishing retreat they need on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Mark, Sheila, Giselle and Shaun – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: More from the day’s top stories and communities across Scotland.

programme.title: Food Fest Scotland
programme.desc: Edith Bowman introduces Colin Murray to her home town of Anstruther on a food adventure. As well as its famous fish and chips, they discover how artisan bread is being made for the community. Farmer Jim Smith tests his tastebuds with some hot sauces and discovers the secrets of marmalade. Chef Julie Lin is in Dundee finding out how bakers keep up with demand around the clock.

programme.title: Born to Be Wild
programme.desc: Head of birds Lorraine is one of the most experienced and dedicated members of the SSPCA rescue centre staff, hand-rearing hundreds of baby nestlings and nursing dozens of injured birds back to health each year. But this is a year like no other, and in mid-March, the lives of the centre staff are turned upside down by the arrival of the coronavirus pandemic. Lorraine is forced to shield at home, but she isn’t going to let the pandemic get in the way of her work. Two collared dove chicks she names Dave and Daisy follow her home, and it isn’t long before she’s also caring for orphaned goldfinches, a concussed robin and even a mute swan, which crash-lands in a field next to Lorraine’s home and is transported straight back to its home on Loch Leven.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Craig Gordon is famous for his resilience and defiance of strikers, coaches, critics and doctors. He has granted BBC cameras unprecedented access to his life over 12 months as, at the age of 42, he makes one last attempt to reach a World Cup. Along the way, we learn about the miracle saves and comebacks from injuries that should have ended his career and that have allowed him to still compete at the top level for so many years. From a prodigy at Hearts to a record breaker in the English Premier League and an invincible at Celtic, Craig Gordon has had a career like no other, but there is one thing still missing - an appearance at a World Cup. To get there, he will have to overcome opposition on the pitch as well as the limitations of his own body as he battles injuries to keep the dream alive. A fascinating insight into the mind of one of Scotland’s most driven athletes.

programme.title: Kevin Bridges: In Search of the Beautiful Game
programme.desc: Kevin Bridges embarks on a journey to see if the beautiful game still exists. He meets Brazil football icon Cafu, Scottish legend John McGinn, Sao Paulo ultras, US football fans and many others.

programme.title: That Was the Team That Was
programme.desc: Scotland's 1974 World Cup team was arguably the best group of Scottish footballers ever assembled and were considered genuine contenders to win the tournament. This is the inside story of that unforgettable summer of football told by the players who represented Scotland in West Germany.

programme.title: Ladhood
programme.desc: Liam is back at his parents’ house in Leeds. Having told Jess he’ll spend the day preparing to perform at a local spoken word night, instead he’s procrastinating and playing old video games. But when he turns on his childhood computer and stumbles on an old homemade hip-hop track, it triggers a memory. Leeds, early noughties. Inspired by the new wave of ‘bedroom musicians’ breaking into the charts, Liam tries to convince his best mates Addy, Craggy and Ralph to make a hip-hop track with him. But when they don’t take “the art” seriously, Liam struggles to keep a lid on it.

programme.title: Ladhood
programme.desc: Liam finds himself doing lines of cocaine at a warehouse party on a Tuesday night with a stranger called Penelope. Realising he has a (long-awaited) mental health assessment the next morning, he plans to go home, but he can’t quite drag himself away. Has he always been this reckless? Leeds, early noughties. Ralph has an empty house during the school half-term. To make the most of this new-found freedom, the lads try to buy weed from the town’s most prolific drug-dealer, Maskill. He quickly informs them his business has changed. He only sells cocaine now. Ralph takes a gram on credit. While Addy and Craggy refuse to try it, Ralph and Liam are swept up in the excitement and invite Rupert and Tinhead over to Ralph’s empty house. When Maskill and a group of strangers turn up to join proceedings, Ralph’s small gathering becomes a big house party. The following morning, Liam wakes up to find that Ralph has run up a serious debt with Maskill, who has taken the family television as a deposit. Can they get the money together in time to repay Ralph’s debt before his parents return home?

programme.title: Ladhood

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: The pressure builds as chicks prepare to fledge and predators close in. The Springwatch team hope to capture even more intimate moments from the lives of the wildlife calling National Trust Crom home through their 24-hour remote camera surveillance. Away from Crom, Iolo Williams spends his final night live at Knepp, where rewilding is transforming the landscape. From free-roaming grazing animals to rare species returning against the odds, Iolo discovers how nature is reclaiming one of Britain’s most ambitious conservation projects.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: A surgeon must remove his patient’s voice box to save his life, while another takes on a life-changing procedure for a patient with a rare auto-immune condition.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: An air ambulance pilot with a taste for adventure is searching for a peaceful home in Northern Ireland where she can truly switch off after high-flying shifts. Originally from New Zealand, Agnieszka has lived an extraordinary life, including time spent in Antarctica, and now has £200,000 to find a place of her own within an hour of Belfast airport. Helping with the search is Briony May Williams, who also squeezes in a spirited Irish dancing lesson on the scenic shores of Lough Neagh.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Chris Hull and Lee Burkhill travel to Coventry to help mother-and-daughter nurses Barbara and Tate transform their completely empty garden into an exotic jungle retreat.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael ends the first leg of his Japan adventure on a Shinkansen bullet train, heading to Nagano, the host city of the 1998 Winter Olympics and the gateway to the Japanese Alps. At the top of the Ryuoo Ropeway, the largest cable car of its type, he takes in the spectacular view and the phenomenon of the ‘sea of clouds'. In the town of Obuse, Michael learns how Japan’s most famous artwork, Hokusai’s The Great Wave off Kanagawa, was made. He visits the largest wasabi farm in the world, where the plants are sheltered from the elements and fed by pure mountain spring water. Finally, he heads to the historic mountain town of Narai Juku, with its beautifully preserved wooden houses.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the final leg of his journey, Michael travels to South Korea’s south west, where food, protest and landscape reveal the values that have shaped the modern nation. Arriving by high-speed train in Gwangju, he explores the region’s deep-rooted food culture, meeting a prizewinning kimchi maker to learn how Korea’s iconic fermented dish has sustained communities for centuries and become a symbol of shared labour and tradition. Michael then confronts a darker chapter in South Korea’s history at the May 18th Memorial Park, where a survivor of the 1980 Gwangju Uprising recounts how student-led protests against military rule were brutally suppressed and why the events are now regarded as the cornerstone of Korean democracy. Leaving the mainland, Michael crosses by ferry to Jeju Island, a volcanic landscape dominated by Mount Halla. Exploring lava tubes with a volcanologist, he uncovers how the island was formed before meeting the Haenyeo, Jeju’s legendary female free divers.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Queen's Tennis
programme.desc: Live coverage from day 3 of the 2026 Queen's tennis tournament.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Simon Armitage, Josie Gibson, Ardal O'Hanlon and Adele Roberts take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure reaches the Dalmatian coastal city of Zadar, once an important Venetian trading hub and still a centre for the production of a Venetian delicacy, maraschino cherry liqueur. In Sibenik, Michael finds one of the first towns in the world to enjoy electric street lighting. At the Krka hydroelectric power station, he discovers how, in the 1890s, the pioneering ideas of the inventor and electrical engineer Nikola Tesla were embraced by the mayor of Sibenik and his son. In the medieval backstreets of Trogir, Michael visits a renowned tailor to try on a traditional Dalmatian suit. He visits the spectacular palace of the Roman emperor Diocletian in Split, and at the Cathedral of St Domnius, he learns of the importance of Catholicism to the Croatian people.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson visits Runswick Bay on the North Yorkshire coast, where he discovers how this pretty village was once a place of danger. Ben explores the mythical ‘hob-holes’ to uncover how they once helped supply a thriving jet industry and finds evidence of how, in the late 1800s, the village became the inspiration for a group of artists who became known as the British Impressionists.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: From coffee-making robots in Japan to bionic limbs in New York, can revolutionary technology transform the lives of millions of disabled people?

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Fridges have been quietly ‘keeping things cool’ in the kitchen for over 100 years, and yet most of us barely give them a second thought. Hannah hits the production line with appliance giants Bosch to find the lifeblood at the heart of every fridge and gets a lesson in carrot droop. And she takes a long, cool look at the fridge’s history to reveal how a French monk with a flair for chemistry, a 17th century chicken incubator and an explosive invention in Australia created the ultimate chill.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan celebrate the season’s standout wildlife moments as Springwatch heads towards its grand finale. Iolo Williams continues his exploration of the spectacular seabird colonies at Bempton Cliffs, where thousands of gannets, guillemots and puffins crowd the towering coastline.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: A surgeon has one chance to tackle a life-threatening tumour in his patient’s liver and diaphragm. A neurosurgeon must save her patient from paralysis with unerring precision.

programme.title: On the Front Line
programme.desc: It started with the seizure of illegal cigarettes hidden in the back room of a minimart in Rochdale and ended with cocaine being bought over the counter from a shop in the West Midlands. Over a year, BBC news investigated the crime happening in plain sight on high streets across the country and, in the process, exposed the crime gangs exploiting the vulnerable and setting up shop in Britain.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: John Simpson, in discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, explores the impact of Israel’s recent attacks on Lebanon, analyses the flotation of SpaceX and what it will mean for Elon Musk, and looks at the outcome of the election in Armenia.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: On 17 August 1996, 21-year-old David Beckham raised his hands to the sky, having just scored against Wimbledon from his own half. That iconic image turned Beckham into a household name and kickstarted a relationship with image-making that would propel the footballer into the popular imagination and help redefine modern celebrity. But behind the popular narrative is a deeper story: of how the footballer used his image to turn himself into a global brand – one that went far beyond the limits of his extraordinary footballing skills – and in so doing helped change attitudes to celebrity, masculinity and class.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure reaches the Dalmatian coastal city of Zadar, once an important Venetian trading hub and still a centre for the production of a Venetian delicacy, maraschino cherry liqueur. In Sibenik, Michael finds one of the first towns in the world to enjoy electric street lighting. At the Krka hydroelectric power station, he discovers how, in the 1890s, the pioneering ideas of the inventor and electrical engineer Nikola Tesla were embraced by the mayor of Sibenik and his son. In the medieval backstreets of Trogir, Michael visits a renowned tailor to try on a traditional Dalmatian suit. He visits the spectacular palace of the Roman emperor Diocletian in Split, and at the Cathedral of St Domnius, he learns of the importance of Catholicism to the Croatian people.

programme.title: In Ten Pictures
programme.desc: On 17 August 1996, 21-year-old David Beckham raised his hands to the sky, having just scored against Wimbledon from his own half. That iconic image turned Beckham into a household name and kickstarted a relationship with image-making that would propel the footballer into the popular imagination and help redefine modern celebrity. But behind the popular narrative is a deeper story: of how the footballer used his image to turn himself into a global brand – one that went far beyond the limits of his extraordinary footballing skills – and in so doing helped change attitudes to celebrity, masculinity and class.

Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are mirrors which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate mirrors inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: A sleepover with their cousin means Bluey and Bingo get to stay up late! But when Muffin shows up exhausted after missing her nap, the girls get more fun than they bargained for.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is distracted from his newspaper because he must warn Roly not to spill his drink and tell Norrie not to drop crumbs; the Squirrels are causing a bit too much mess, so Duggee teaches them an important lesson. The Squirrels learn that there are certain dos and don’ts that you must follow in order to avoid mess or getting hurt, but that you can still have fun along the way. Knowing why they should listen to these rules helps them understand their importance - if you spill your drink, someone could slip, and leftover crumbs can attract unwelcome guests. The Squirrels take turns suggesting their dos and don’ts, but some are a bit more niche than others. But most importantly, they remember that you do have fun with your friends!

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Yellow is happy to bring his colour to Colourland. Learn about the colour yellow with the Colourblocks.

Rory and his son Sandy go hunting for woodlice in the park and build a bug hotel, while Ferne learns that woodlice are crustaceans just like crayfish. Plus, we find out how woodlice are great for the environment – they are little eco-engineers!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie plan a woodland adventure. They create a list of all the things they’d like to see and find and pack some snacks for their intrepid journey. On their adventure with Mum and Dad, they discover colourful leaves, trees to climb, and bugs under rocks. But will they escape the treacherous troll hiding under the bridge? Back at home, there’s time for a warming cup of hot chocolate before settling down to bed.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Leo's family is from Russia, and they have shown him how to make a special sharlotka, a simple Russian apple cake. Leo starts by separating the eggs. He then adds sugar and flour to the yolks and mixes them together until the mixture is smooth. He whisks the egg whites until they are stiff and stirs them into the yolk mix. After this, Leo cuts apples into small chunks and places half of them in a cake tin, pours over the egg mixture and puts the rest of the apples on top. Then the sharlotka is ready to be baked in the oven. Leo even has an extra special Russian-themed surprise for his friends while they eat! Can they work out what his special ingredient is?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Today, Maddie is having fun by the beach! She finds out how waves are formed far out to sea when the wind blows and how some of them are made by the tides. She visits a surfing centre and takes to the waves on a surfboard. Maddie attaches her special cameras to the surfboard to learn how the energy underneath the wave can carry us along and how when it reaches the shore the wave slows down and breaks. Next, Maddie visits a dairy farm and finds out how milk from cows is made into ice cream. She uses a special thermometer to show how cold the ice cream mixture is when it comes out of the batch freezer and turns from a liquid to a solid.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Disability assistance dog Tinks needs all her super fetch skills and big dog energy as she helps Charli catch a bus to meet her friend Lydia, who is getting married.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet Obi, the spectacled bear. He gets his name from the light-coloured markings in the fur around his face that look like spectacles. The keepers have hidden fruit in his enclosure, and they watch as he searches for his breakfast. Obi stands high on his back legs to reach it in the trees, then uses his large claws to pick fruit from the water. Next, they head out to see the largest of all the big cats – the tiger. They meet Miron and reveal that every tiger has its own unique pattern of stripes – no two tigers look the same. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog

All while Otti tries to avoid playing with the boat whistle! They are all directed towards a mysterious-looking cave where Chew Chew is waiting for both parcels. They deliver them at the same time, but they contain different things – one is full of biscuits and the other organic almond milk. They aren’t the same but they go really well together, just like the Squirrels and Hummingbirds!

Along the way, he battles with a polar allosaurus, one of Australia's deadliest predators, as well as witnessing cute antics from baby leaellynasaura. Will Andy succeed before the museum opens?

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies are flamenco dancing! Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po are surprisingly good.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Ferne, Roman, Rosa-May, Sehaj, Benjamin, Elias, Isobel and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are mirrors which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding safe, baby appropriate mirrors inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Baby Bear Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children craft rainsticks, learn British Sign Language signs for thunder, wet and raindrops, then sing and sign the stormy rhyme, I Hear Thunder.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Heritage seed expert Lucy and the Fact Pack explore the colourful world of heritage tomatoes and discover why eating different-coloured fruits and vegetables is good for us.

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: Twiggy the giraffe spends some time by herself. Hamza spots some incredible black rhinos in the wild and helps Ronald the vet give Thompson’s gazelle Ruka a check-up.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger must navigate chaos amid rolling Coconutdons and tail-swatting Pineapplesauruses.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: A sleepover with their cousin means Bluey and Bingo get to stay up late! But when Muffin shows up exhausted after missing her nap, the girls get more fun than they bargained for.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is distracted from his newspaper because he must warn Roly not to spill his drink and tell Norrie not to drop crumbs; the Squirrels are causing a bit too much mess, so Duggee teaches them an important lesson. The Squirrels learn that there are certain dos and don’ts that you must follow in order to avoid mess or getting hurt, but that you can still have fun along the way. Knowing why they should listen to these rules helps them understand their importance - if you spill your drink, someone could slip, and leftover crumbs can attract unwelcome guests. The Squirrels take turns suggesting their dos and don’ts, but some are a bit more niche than others. But most importantly, they remember that you do have fun with your friends!

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Yellow is happy to bring his colour to Colourland. Learn about the colour yellow with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Teeny Tiny Creatures
programme.desc: Today, Himmat wants to learn about wonderful woodlice! Rory and his son Sandy go hunting for woodlice in the park and build a bug hotel, while Ferne learns that woodlice are crustaceans just like crayfish. Plus, we find out how woodlice are great for the environment – they are little eco-engineers!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: George and Freddie plan a woodland adventure. They create a list of all the things they’d like to see and find and pack some snacks for their intrepid journey. On their adventure with Mum and Dad, they discover colourful leaves, trees to climb, and bugs under rocks. But will they escape the treacherous troll hiding under the bridge? Back at home, there’s time for a warming cup of hot chocolate before settling down to bed.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Leo's family is from Russia, and they have shown him how to make a special sharlotka, a simple Russian apple cake. Leo starts by separating the eggs. He then adds sugar and flour to the yolks and mixes them together until the mixture is smooth. He whisks the egg whites until they are stiff and stirs them into the yolk mix. After this, Leo cuts apples into small chunks and places half of them in a cake tin, pours over the egg mixture and puts the rest of the apples on top. Then the sharlotka is ready to be baked in the oven. Leo even has an extra special Russian-themed surprise for his friends while they eat! Can they work out what his special ingredient is?

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Today, Maddie is having fun by the beach! She finds out how waves are formed far out to sea when the wind blows and how some of them are made by the tides. She visits a surfing centre and takes to the waves on a surfboard. Maddie attaches her special cameras to the surfboard to learn how the energy underneath the wave can carry us along and how when it reaches the shore the wave slows down and breaks. Next, Maddie visits a dairy farm and finds out how milk from cows is made into ice cream. She uses a special thermometer to show how cold the ice cream mixture is when it comes out of the batch freezer and turns from a liquid to a solid.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Disability assistance dog Tinks needs all her super fetch skills and big dog energy as she helps Charli catch a bus to meet her friend Lydia, who is getting married.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet Obi, the spectacled bear. He gets his name from the light-coloured markings in the fur around his face that look like spectacles. The keepers have hidden fruit in his enclosure, and they watch as he searches for his breakfast. Obi stands high on his back legs to reach it in the trees, then uses his large claws to pick fruit from the water. Next, they head out to see the largest of all the big cats – the tiger. They meet Miron and reveal that every tiger has its own unique pattern of stripes – no two tigers look the same. These two animals are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between them.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: It's a hot summer's day in Higgledy Piggledy, and Granny is taking Maddie and Triggs to visit Mr Moon's shop for a treat. Maddie is confused because the shop doesn't seem like much fun. But Mr Moon has more than a few surprises and tasty treats up his sleeve!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: As Peggee and the Hummingbirds journey up the river to deliver a parcel, they have fun spotting and avoiding the wildlife that they meet along the way. All while Otti tries to avoid playing with the boat whistle! The Hummingbirds see the likes of meerkats, an aye-aye and snapping turtles and soon bump into some friendly faces - Duggee and the Squirrels! They are delivering a parcel upstream too. They reach their destination at the same time, and Otti and Roly finally get to sound the boat whistle. They are all directed towards a mysterious-looking cave where Chew Chew is waiting for both parcels. They deliver them at the same time, but they contain different things – one is full of biscuits and the other organic almond milk. They aren’t the same but they go really well together, just like the Squirrels and Hummingbirds!

programme.title: Keane & Vieira - Best of Enemies
programme.desc: Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira hated each other - Keane described himself as being 'in a war' with Vieira, and their infamous tunnel bust-up in February 2005 has entered folklore. They fought on the pitch and they tried to fight off of it, but most fans would agree that Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira were the two footballing warriors that defined their age. In this explosive documentary, the two men come together to explain why they hated each other, what they really thought of Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger, and what it means to be the best of enemies.

programme.desc: Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira hated each other - Keane described himself as being 'in a war' with Vieira, and their infamous tunnel bust-up in February 2005 has entered folklore. They fought on the pitch and they tried to fight off of it, but most fans would agree that Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira were the two footballing warriors that defined their age. In this explosive documentary, the two men come together to explain why they hated each other, what they really thought of Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger, and what it means to be the best of enemies.

Elsewhere, vet Amy performs surgery to remove a lump from King Charles Spaniel Eddie, James neuters a dog called Barney who has been rescued from Macedonia, Fern helps out when young Cavapoo Mila gets preventative treatment, and we find out about the work of the Holly Hedge Animal Sanctuary which rehomes 400 cats and dogs each year.

programme.title: Keane & Vieira - Best of Enemies
programme.desc: Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira hated each other - Keane described himself as being 'in a war' with Vieira, and their infamous tunnel bust-up in February 2005 has entered folklore. They fought on the pitch and they tried to fight off of it, but most fans would agree that Roy Keane and Patrick Vieira were the two footballing warriors that defined their age. In this explosive documentary, the two men come together to explain why they hated each other, what they really thought of Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsene Wenger, and what it means to be the best of enemies.

programme.desc: The iconic TV series is back, but in a brand-new setting with brand-new prize boxes and a new batch of contestants hoping to win a whopping cash prize - who will have what it takes to beat our brand-new Banker? Now hosted by Stephen Mulhern, the series will see contestants battle it out against the notorious Banker to be in with a chance of winning a life-changing cash prize in a nail-biting game of nerves and intuition. Contestants are confronted with 22 sealed boxes with each one hiding a different amount of money - without knowing what each one contains, the contestant must eliminate the boxes, which are opened one at a time, and the amount of money inside is revealed. Pressure mounts as the player is tempted by the notorious Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for what might be inside their box, and as long as the larger cash prizes remain unchosen, the Banker's offers will get higher... but that can all change in an instant if a big cash prize is unveiled.
